final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and instead narrowed the claim using the same record. That narrowing is useful but not curative. It supports a more accurate description of the dispute: aggregate launch readiness may be supported, while the materiality and disclosure issue remains contested. Under the stated policy, however, that contest is itself a compliance predicate. The available record still shows a gap in a segment named in two paid pilot commitments and an open legal review, with no evidence of resolved disclosure, approved risk acceptance, or legal closure before launch. That means the caveat is not merely a disclosure note within an otherwise compliant certification; it is an unresolved condition for compliance. Public governance guidance remains supplementary and does not replace the internal policy requirement.
remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence shows the small-business onboarding limitation was disclosed for the named pilot commitments or launch materials.
No new admissible evidence shows an approved risk acceptance covering this material weakness before launch.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required remains open, so a stated policy predicate is still unresolved.
The policy text says a weakness is material when it affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case; the summary says this segment is named in two paid pilot commitments.
Aggregate readiness and lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents do not satisfy the internal disclosure/risk-acceptance requirement for a material weakness.
